newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Housewares falls on earnings worries.
newsitem.headline: Housewares falls on earnings worries.

text.p: South African household goods and mail order firm Housewares Ltd fell on Friday after the firm warned on current year profits and posted a drop in year earnings per share.
By 0745 GMT the stock had lost 22 cents, or 13.5 percent, to a new year low of 140 cents -- making it the fourth biggest loser in percentage terms on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
After the close of trade on Thursday Housewares posted year headline earnings per share down to 17.4 cents, against 28.3 cents last time.
The firm blamed a harsh credit environment for the fall in earnings especially in the direct sales business, and said it considered it prudent not to declare a dividend.
The group also said it was unlikely to show improved earnings in the new financial year as there was little indication that the retail credit environment would improve in the short term.
"Things are looking very tough in its markets," one dealer said.

However, on the bright side Housewares said its mail order unit Glomail had done well and it also planned to "right size" the sales division and reduce overhead costs. At the same time its information technology would be enhanced.
